sops.SOP-01 Shutdown response: A protective shutdown stops equipment because a limit was reached or an instrument disagrees with the process. Establish the cause before restarting. Unexplained trips require field verification (dispatch a technician).
sops.SOP-02 Protective function bypass: Bypassing a protective shutdown or the station ESD is an abnormal-situation measure. It requires a verified cause and supervisor authority, must be time-limited and removed as soon as possible, and must be recorded in the shift log.
sops.SOP-03 Shift log: The shift log must state every abnormal event, every alarm inhibited, every bypass applied or requested, every setpoint or valve change made outside normal operation, and the reason for each.

Expect reduced station throughput until U2 is cleared.

text:
SHIFT LOG – 4:00 PM to 7:00 PM. Cold snap, ambient about 16-23F (rising).

START (4:00): U1/U2/U3 running at 80% load. No alarms or work orders. Gas control asked for all units fully loaded through peak (~9 PM). Note: in the first sample STATION.flow showed 0.0 and ambient showed 70F. Both went to believable values (about 27 MMSCFD, 15F) within 5 minutes. This looks like stale or initializing data, but please have I&E check these transmitters.

4:00-4:15: Raised all units 80 -> 90 -> 100%. The discharge header climbed from 1001 to 1055 psig at about 4 psi/min with flow of only about 30 MMSCFD. At 4:11, ALM-001/002/003 came in on U1/U2/U3 (high discharge pressure pre-trip, about 1037 psig). To avoid tripping all three units, I cut them to 85% at 4:15 and the header settled near 1025. I told gas control the downstream side was not taking the gas. Alarms were acknowledged, not inhibited.

4:20-4:33 U2 HIGH JACKET WATER: U2 jacket water rose from 161F to 192F at about 2.5F/min. ALM-004 (U2 high jacket temp pre-trip) came in at about 4:28 and was acknowledged. U1/U3 stayed normal at about 161F. At 4:30 I cut U2 to 60% and dispatched the on-call tech (TECH-1, urgent). The temperature kept rising. At 4:33 I did a controlled stop of U2 before it reached the trip or damaged the engine. NO bypass was requested or applied. Gas control was told. Afterwards I ran U1/U3 at 95%, then 100%. With U2 down the header dropped to about 820 psig. At 4:55 gas control asked to keep U2 up; it stayed down until the cause was found and fixed.

5:30: TECH-1 found the U2 cooler fan belt shredded and replaced it. Cooling confirmed normal and U2 cleared to restart. I restarted U2 at 5:30 and loaded it 70% -> 100%. Its jacket water levelled off at about 162F. Gas control was told.

5:35-6:05: With all three at 100%, the header climbed again at 6-9 psi/min toward the pre-trip. I trimmed all units to 92% (5:53), then 88% (6:05). The header has held at about 1015 psig ever since, with flow about 26.5 MMSCFD. Gas control was told that higher throughput needs more downstream takeaway.

END (6:50): U1/U2/U3 all running at 88%. Discharge header about 1016 psig, suction 400 psig. Jacket water about 163F on all units, rod load about 75%. No active alarms. No inhibits, bypasses, setpoint changes or valve changes this shift.

FOLLOW-UP: (1) Check the cooler fan belts and tensioners on U1/U3, and find out why the U2 belt failed. (2) Check the flow and ambient transmitters from the startup glitch. (3) Peak runs to about 9 PM. Keep watching the header against the high discharge pressure pre-trip (about 1037). If gas control wants full load, the downstream side needs to take more gas. (4) TECH-1 call-out (urgent) to be charged.
